newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed strongly on Friday, buoyed by Bunds, as comments by senior Bundesbank figures went some way to allaying market pessimism that German interest rates may have bottomed out.

Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing, who spiked bond market guns on Wednesday by saying there was no reason for further cuts in German rates, moderated his tone on Friday saying future cuts could not be totally ruled out.
He was echoed by fellow Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke, who said another repo rate cut could be possible in the medium term.
The comments spurred Bunds and dealers said that with the market directionless, Guilders were able to notch up strong gains in fairly light trade.
Further predicted flattening of the yield curve failed to materialise, they said, and the 5-10 year spread inched out one basis point.

Bund strength also helped Dutch bonds weather data showing the strongest monthly rise in U.S. durable goods orders in nearly four years. September durables orders rose 4.6 percent after declining a revised 3.5 percent in August.
While overall volumes remained quite subdued, there was fair interest in the 2002 to 2003 area of the yield curve, one dealer said. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
